title: El Niño Will Challenge the New Andean Right
gist: Peruvian researcher Jorge Morel Salman argues that a potentially record El Niño, peaking November to March, will hit exactly as two narrowly elected right-wing presidents take office — Keiko Fujimori in Peru (July 28) and Abelardo De La Espriella in Colombia (August 7). Peru's central bank sees a 0.9pp hit to 2027 GDP against a business consensus of 4%+ growth, while Colombia, where hydropower is over two-thirds of generation and which lost investment grade in 2021, faces rationing and blackout risk with no fiscal cushion.

insights.claim: Water temperatures near Paita in northern Peru were 14.2 degrees Fahrenheit above average in June, with Peruvian climate agencies expecting this year's El Niño to be especially strong from November through next March.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: A 14.2°F anomaly this early points to a severe event; the Nov-March window is the concrete timing for agricultural, fishing and logistics disruption trades.
insights.quote: Near the city of Paita, in northern Peru, water temperatures were already a stunning 14.2 degrees Fahrenheit above average in June.
insights.locator: Near the city of Paita

insights.claim: The forecast pattern for Peru is geographically split — flooding in the north, drought in the south, and disruptive heat on the coast — meaning the shock hits different sectors through different mechanisms simultaneously.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: A single-direction weather hedge misses the structure; northern flooding hits fruit and infrastructure while southern drought hits food supply chains and prices.
insights.quote: foreseeing flooding in the north, drought in the south, and disruptive heat on the coast
insights.locator: Near the city of Paita

insights.claim: Climate models assign a 99% probability that El Niño conditions persist in Colombia through September and a 63% probability they intensify from November to January.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Near-certainty of persistence with a 63% intensification odds makes Colombian power-supply stress a high-probability event, not a tail risk.
insights.quote: climate models assign a 99% chance that they will persist through September and a 63% probability that they will intensify from November to January
insights.locator: El Niño conditions are already present

insights.claim: Peru is currently experiencing a "Coastal El Niño" that is expected to overlap with the broader oceanic El Niño later this year, and if the two combine severely they would batter the infrastructure sustaining Peru's domestic and international trade.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: The overlap scenario is the tail case — port, road and logistics disruption in Peru would transmit to copper and agricultural export volumes.
insights.quote: These current effects are the work of the “Coastal El Niño,” which is expected to overlap with the broader oceanic El Niño later this year.

themes.theme: Peru's macro hit versus consensus optimism

insights.claim: Peru's central bank estimates El Niño could subtract nearly a full percentage point — 0.9% — from 2027 GDP growth, while the Instituto Peruano de Economía projects a 0.8% impact.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Two independent 0.8-0.9pp GDP drag estimates give a quantified downside to Peruvian growth forecasts and, by extension, to fiscal revenue and PEN.
insights.quote: Peru’s BRCP, as the central bank is known, estimates that El Niño could subtract nearly a full percentage point—0.9%—from GDP growth in 2027, while the Instituto Peruano de Economía projects the impact at 0.8%.
insights.locator: A range of threats

insights.claim: Peruvian business expectations captured in the central bank's June Macroeconomic Expectations Survey put GDP growth above 4%, a level the author argues El Niño could dash — implying consensus is not pricing the climate drag.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: A gap between a 4%+ business consensus and a quantified 0.9pp climate drag is the tradeable dislocation — position for downward revisions to Peruvian growth.
insights.quote: Many expect GDP growth above 4%, but those hopes could be dashed by El Niño.
insights.locator: Fujimori will start her term

insights.claim: High ocean temperatures had by early March already destroyed roughly 6,000 hectares of fruit in northern Peru, disrupting mango, blueberry and avocado harvests and damaging the fishing industry.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Peru is a dominant global supplier in blueberries and avocados; 6,000 destroyed hectares before the event even peaks points to upside in those soft-commodity prices.
insights.quote: By early March, they had destroyed roughly 6,000 hectares of fruit in the northern part of the country, and they have likewise hurt the fishing industry.
insights.locator: High ocean temperatures have already disrupted

insights.claim: The Lima Chamber of Commerce estimates El Niño could generate potential losses of more than $80 million per day across seven exposed Peruvian regions later this year.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: An $80m/day loss run-rate frames the scale — roughly $2.4bn a month of exposure, enough to move Peru's fiscal and current-account arithmetic.
insights.quote: The Lima Chamber of Commerce has estimated that El Niño could generate potential losses of more than $80 million per day across seven exposed regions later this year.
insights.locator: The Lima Chamber of Commerce

insights.claim: The transmission mechanism runs through damaged assets, delayed shipments and higher transport costs for businesses, and through lower production and exports, rising food prices and emergency public spending for the macro economy — with southern drought an under-appreciated additional food-price driver.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Points to a simultaneous growth-down, inflation-up shock in Peru — a policy bind for the BRCP if food inflation reaccelerates into a growth slowdown.
insights.quote: Moreover, a serious drought in the south—a risk that has received less attention from policymakers—could inflate food prices further.
insights.locator: Businesses would contend with damaged assets

insights.claim: Northern Peru remains as vulnerable to flooding as it was in 2017 because recovery efforts have been beset by delays, weak oversight and irregularities — meaning nearly a decade of reconstruction spending bought no resilience.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Zero improvement in physical resilience means 2017-scale damage is the correct baseline for the 2026-27 event, not a discounted figure.
insights.quote: The 2017 El Niño left several cities under water, and all these years later, northern Peru remains just as vulnerable to flooding because recovery efforts have been beset by delays, weak oversight, and irregularities.
insights.locator: The 2017 El Niño left several cities

insights.claim: Peru's Comptroller General reported in 2023 that 120 reconstruction projects representing over $900 million in investment were stalled nationwide, and a separate Piura review identified 131 officials with potential criminal, civil and administrative responsibility for irregularities.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: $900m of stalled projects and 131 implicated officials quantify the execution-capacity constraint — new emergency budgets are unlikely to convert into physical protection.
insights.quote: The Comptroller General reported in 2023 that 120 reconstruction projects representing over $900 million in investment were stalled nationwide
insights.locator: The 2017 El Niño left several cities

insights.claim: Southern drought poses a harder governance problem than northern flooding because it demands keeping food and water supply chains functioning rather than rebuilding, a task a brand-new government cannot address quickly.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Drought response requires logistics competence rather than capex — a capability new administrations typically lack, raising the odds of visible failure.
insights.quote: In the south, drought would create less demand for rebuilding than for keeping food and water supply chains functioning, problems that would be difficult for a new government to address quickly.

themes.theme: Colombia's power grid and fiscal fragility

insights.claim: Hydropower supplies more than two-thirds of Colombia's electricity generation, so El Niño-driven drought depleting reservoirs raises the specter of rationing and blackouts like the rolling outages that hit Ecuador in 2024.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: The Ecuador 2024 precedent is the template — Colombian utilities, thermal generators and industrial power consumers should be repriced for rationing risk.
insights.quote: In Colombia, a country where hydropower supplies more than two-thirds of electricity generation, forecasters predict droughts that will deplete reservoirs and threaten the electrical system.
insights.locator: In Colombia, a country where hydropower

insights.claim: Colombia's risk exposure is greater than Peru's because it lost investment grade in 2021 and therefore has little room to borrow cheaply, while Peru has maintained investment grade despite volatility.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: The clearest relative-value call in the piece: a climate shock requiring emergency spending is materially more damaging to Colombian credit than to Peruvian — favor Peru over Colombia in Andean sovereign risk.
insights.quote: Having lost its investment grade in 2021, Colombia has little room to borrow with cheap credit, while Peru has maintained investment grade despite its ups and downs.
insights.locator: The risks are especially high for Colombia

insights.claim: Colombia's weather agency warns reduced rainfall and higher temperatures could restrict drinking water, damage crops and livestock, increase wildfires and worsen health risks tied to air quality, heat and mosquitoes — a multi-channel shock beyond electricity.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Broadens Colombian El Niño exposure beyond utilities into food inflation and health-system spending, compounding an already tight fiscal position.
insights.quote: reduced rainfall and higher temperatures could also restrict drinking-water supplies, damage crops and livestock, increase wildfires, and worsen health risks related to air quality, heat, and mosquitoes
insights.locator: The government’s weather agency warns

insights.claim: Environment Minister-designate Fabio Arjona has indicated the incoming Colombian administration will permit limited fracking, a position that could become a political flashpoint if acute water stress materializes.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: A concrete signal that Colombia is reopening to unconventional hydrocarbons — bullish for Colombian upstream, but the water-stress collision creates permitting and protest risk.
insights.quote: Environment Minister-designate Fabio Arjona has indicated that the administration will permit limited fracking. If acute water stress materializes, that position could become an additional political flashpoint.
insights.locator: The government’s weather agency warns

insights.claim: Keiko Fujimori won Peru's June presidential runoff by less than three-tenths of a percentage point over her leftist rival and will govern with a fragmented Congress precisely when disaster management demands speed.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: A sub-0.3pp mandate plus a fragmented legislature means low capacity to pass emergency measures — elevated Peruvian political-instability risk within the first year.
insights.quote: she won the June presidential runoff by less than three-tenths of a point over her leftist rival
insights.locator: All this could stymie growth

insights.claim: Both Andean presidents take office immediately before the climate peak — Fujimori on July 28 and De La Espriella on August 7 — so their first six months in office are likely to coincide with intense climate events that will define their political fortunes.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Calendar alignment means no honeymoon period; approval-rating deterioration is likely in H1 of both terms, raising governability risk premia in both markets.
insights.quote: If most El Niño models are correct, the two presidents’ first six months in office are likely to see intense climate events.
insights.locator: These challenges will greet new governments

insights.claim: Natural disasters open a corruption flank because they trigger emergency purchases, budget reallocations and expedited borrowing, contracting and reconstruction programs that are especially vulnerable to graft and fraud.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Expect procurement scandals as a second-order political risk in both countries within 12 months, independent of the physical damage itself.
insights.quote: Natural disasters can trigger emergency purchases, budget reallocations, and expedited borrowing, contracting, and reconstruction programs that are especially vulnerable to graft and fraud.
insights.locator: A parallel problem

insights.claim: After the 1997-1998 El Niño, Alberto Fujimori's highly publicized personal aid deliveries initially lifted his approval three to four points before public perception in affected areas deteriorated as the centralized, personalized response failed — a precedent the author says could backfire even more acutely for today's fragile mandates.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: A direct historical template with a quantified approval arc: a short 3-4 point bounce followed by reversal — fade any early disaster-response popularity gains for both leaders.
insights.quote: Polls initially showed his approval rising three to four points, but as flooding intensified and the failures of the government’s highly centralized and personalized approach to aid became more apparent
insights.locator: After the devastating 1997-1998 El Niño

insights.claim: Disaster funds create clientelist temptation — money can be steered to electorally valuable districts, allies rewarded with resources, and public initiatives portrayed as personal presidential favors.
insights.speaker: JORGE MOREL SALMAN
insights.so_what: Political allocation of reconstruction spending reduces its economic multiplier — discount headline stimulus figures for both countries.
insights.quote: Funds can be driven toward electorally valuable districts, allies can be awarded with resources, and public initiatives can be portrayed as personal favors granted by the president.
insights.locator: And simple clientelism has its own tempting logic.
